samples.summary: No test covers the `created_at ?? 0` fallback in ciPassed's comparator (missing/unparseable timestamp)
samples.evidence: The new test at mark-ready.test.mjs:211-247 exercises the comparator only with two well-formed, distinct ISO timestamps. The production comparator at mark-ready.mjs:136 explicitly defends against absent timestamps (`new Date(b.created_at ?? 0)`), and an unparseable string (e.g. "yesterday") yields NaN, making the comparator return NaN and leaving the ordering effectively arbitrary — so a red-but-undated newest CI run could still promote. That defensive branch, and the equal-timestamp tie case, are both untested; every fixture in the suite supplies a valid, unique `created_at`. Contained impact (the fallback only matters on malformed API data), but it is real fake-free coverage that is missing.

samples.summary: Newest-run test does not cover the common real case: an in-progress (conclusion null) re-run newer than an older green run
samples.evidence: mark-ready.test.mjs:171-182 tests `conclusion: null` only as the sole run. The new newest-run test (211-247) uses only success/failure pairs. The practically frequent scenario — CI re-run queued/in-progress (conclusion null) while an older run is green — is exactly the state where a broken comparator would promote an unverified head. It is implied by the two tested cases but not asserted directly, so a change that special-cased null (e.g. skipping null-conclusion runs before sorting) would keep the suite green while promoting on stale evidence.

finding.summary: No test covers "latest CI run wins" — the re-run sort in ciPassed is unexercised
finding.evidence: The new test "gate 1 reads the run NAMED 'CI'" pins the `r.name === "CI"` filter but never gives two CI runs with different `created_at`. Across the whole suite every config has at most one `{name: "CI", ...}` entry (mark-ready.test.mjs:89, 174-176, 193, 205); the second run in the new test is named `agent-review-panel` and is filtered out before the sort. So `runs.sort((a,b) => new Date(b.created_at) - new Date(a.created_at))` at mark-ready.mjs:136 has no coverage: inverting the comparator (or dropping the sort) keeps every test green while an OLD green CI run stands in for a NEWER red one, promoting a PR whose CI actually failed — exactly the unforgeable-evidence guard this file exists to enforce.

verdict.reason: The claimed-missing test exists in the very file the reviewer says they read in full. scripts/agent/mark-ready.test.mjs:211-247 is a dedicated test, "gate 1 reads the NEWEST CI run — a stale green one does not outrank a fresh red one", whose fixtures supply TWO runs both named "CI" for the same SHA with different created_at values (older=2026-08-22T00:00:00Z, newer=2026-08-22T09:00:00Z). It asserts both directions: an older green + newer red must exit 1 and never call `gh pr ready` (lines 221-231), and an older red + newer green must exit 0 and actually promote (lines 236-246). This directly exercises the comparator at mark-ready.mjs:136 — inverting it or deleting the sort makes `wentRed` read the stale green run and exit 0, failing assert.equal(wentRed.code, 1); and the converse case prevents the "refuse whenever >1 CI run" cheat from satisfying the first assertion. The finding's factual claims are wrong: "every config has at most one {name: 'CI'} entry" is contradicted by lines 224-227 and 240-243, and the "second run is named agent-review-panel" describes the preceding test at line 189, not this one. The exact harm described (old green standing in for a newer red, promoting a red-CI PR) is the asserted `wentRed` case.
